Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Intake Brief: Challenges as achievements — sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements

## Problem statement

The engine's challenge system (per-run meta-goals, e.g. Main Street's "Foodie Row") is conceptually a form of achievement. Once the Steam version exists (Electron launcher with Steamworks), challenge completions should sync to Steam achievements so players earn persistent, account-level recognition visible on their Steam profile and in the overlay.

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn Steam achievements for completing in-game challenges; see progress on their Steam profile.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — an engine-generic achievement layer so any game can map its challenges to Steam achievements without writing Steam SDK code.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want the challenges I complete in Main Street (and future games) to appear as Steam achievements, so my progress is recognised beyond the run itself.
- As a TCE developer, I want a game-agnostic achievement layer in the engine, so adding achievements to a new game is declarative (challenge → achievement mapping) with no Steam SDK code in the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An **engine-generic achievement layer** exists in the core engine (extending the existing generic `ChallengeSystem` model): games define achievement definitions (id, title, description, hidden flag) and map challenge completions to achievements. This layer is pure engine code with no Steam dependency (works headless / in the web build).
2. When a challenge is completed inside the Steam launcher, the mapped Steam achievement is unlocked via Steamworks (`ISteamUserStats::SetAchievement` + `StoreStats`); verified by automated tests with a mocked Steamworks session and a documented manual E2E check with a real Steam account.
3. Steam sync is **idempotent and offline-safe**: unlocked achievements persist locally, are re-synced to Steam when available, and the launcher never crashes when Steam/Steamworks is absent (graceful degradation, consistent with the follow-on-Steam feature CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
4. A single **achievement manifest** (game id ↔ achievement id ↔ Steam API name, hidden flag) is the source of truth and matches the static Steam store configuration; mismatch detection is documented.
5. **Main Street is the first consumer**: all 12 challenge templates (`MainStreetChallenges.ts`) are mapped to Steam achievements through the generic layer (no Steam SDK code in the game module).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Timing:** Steam sync is implemented only when the Steam version exists — blocked by the Electron launcher (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) and the Steamworks integration introduced by the follow-on-Steam incentive (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC). The engine-generic achievement layer itself can be designed/built now; the Steam bridge lands with Steamworks.
- **Engine-generic (user decision):** no game-specific Steam code; games declare achievements via the generic layer; Main Street first.
- **Steam backend reality:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steam store backend with static API names (App ID + achievement list). The manifest must match that configuration; store setup itself lives outside this repo.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies (Steamworks SDK usage follows the pattern set by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).

## Existing state

- `src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts` — generic `ChallengeDefinition<TState>` / `ActiveChallengeRecord<TState>` interfaces plus generic selection/evaluation; game-agnostic by design ("M6 extraction" notes already anticipate reuse).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — the only consumer: 12 challenge templates across 5 categories, per-run selection (`selectChallenges`), evaluation with completion callback that pushes to `state.challengesCompleted` and the activity log. Challenges are run-local and non-persistent.
- No achievements, no Steam SDK code, no Electron code in the repo today. Steamworks integration is being introduced by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC into the launcher from CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW.
- CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC explicitly defers this scope: "Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item."

## Desired change

1. Add an **achievement concept to the core engine** (new module, e.g. `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`, or an extension of `ChallengeSystem`): achievement definitions, a completion-event surface, and a persistence-agnostic "unlock" registry that the web build can use without Steam.
2. Define the **achievement manifest** for the launcher (`electron/steam-achievements.ts`): game/achievement ids ↔ Steam API names + hidden flags, documented to match the Steam store backend config.
3. Add the **Steam bridge** in the Electron main process: renderer reports achievement-unlocked events via preload/IPC; main process calls Steamworks `SetAchievement`/`StoreStats`; local persistence of unlocked ids with later re-sync; graceful degradation without Steam.
4. **Wire Main Street** as the first consumer: a declarative mapping from the 12 challenge templates to Steam achievements, fired from the existing challenge-completion path.
5. Tests (mocked Steamworks session; headless unit tests for the engine layer) + documentation (README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md` as needed).

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts` (new) — generic achievement definitions + unlock registry + completion-event surface (no Steam dependency).
- `src/core-engine/index.ts` — barrel exports for the new module.
- `electron/steam-achievements.ts` (new) — achievement manifest (ids ↔ Steam API names) + Steamworks sync bridge.
- `electron/main.ts`, `electron/preload.ts` — IPC surface for achievement-unlock events from the renderer.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` (or a new `MainStreetAchievements.ts`) — mapping of the 12 challenge templates to achievements.
- `tests/` — unit tests (engine layer, manifest matching) + mocked-Steamworks sync tests.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md` — Steam achievements workflow documentation.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC – Follow-on-Steam incentive: unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher** (open, intake_complete) — introduces Steamworks SDK integration into the Electron launcher; explicitly defers achievements as a follow-up; its Steamworks setup (init, app ID, mock strategy) is a prerequisite and pattern for this item.
- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, plan_complete) — the "Steam version"; provides the Electron main/preload and DLC content architecture this feature plugs into.
- **CG-0MSMGKVSS000ZEDL – Achievement give-aways: unlock three games when achievements are achieved** (open, idea) — separate item that consumes this item's achievement events as unlock triggers.
- `src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts` — the generic challenge model this feature generalises.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Steam version" means the Electron launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW / CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC.
- **Assumption:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steamworks backend (static API names); the manifest must match that config — coordination with Steam store setup (outside repo) is required before release.
- **Risk:** Challenge completion is currently in-memory/run-local; exposing it as a durable, replayable event (via the existing transcript/event infrastructure) is needed for reliable sync — mitigation: build the completion-event surface in the engine layer first.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module packaging complexity — reuse the approach validated by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam cloud saves, non-binary stat tracking, trading cards, and wishlist prompts are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the challenge→achievement layer be engine-generic (any game's challenges can map to Steam achievements, Main Street first) or only cover Main Street for now?" — Answer (user): "engine-generic". Source: interactive reply (2026-08-09). Implication: the layer is a core-engine module; Main Street is the first consumer.
- Q2: "When should the Steam sync be built?" — Answer (user): per the intake request, "when the steam version has been created these achievements should sync with Steam achievements." Implication: implementation of the Steam bridge is gated on the launcher + Steamworks items; the engine abstraction is not.
- OPEN QUESTION: The exact Steam achievement list/API names for the store backend (business/backend decision outside the repo) — the manifest defines them in one place; the store config must match.

# Intake Brief: Achievement give-aways — unlock three games when achievements are achieved

## Problem statement

To reward engaged players, three games from the TCE catalog will be given away free when players achieve certain achievements in the Steam launcher. The unlock uses the **same game-agnostic mechanism** as the free game awarded for following on Steam (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC): bundled content locked by default, unlocked in place, persisted across launches.

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn free games as a reward for reaching achievements; a reason to keep playing.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — a growth/engagement mechanic that drives play without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want a free game to unlock in my launcher once I've won my first game and reached one more milestone, so my progress is rewarded.
- As a publisher, I want achievement give-aways delivered through the existing bundled-content/unlock architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Three games are selected** from the TCE catalog for achievement give-away; the selection is a documented business decision (Main Street is a noted candidate; selection avoids overlap with the follow-on-Steam bonus game choice — see Related work) and the chosen set + rationale is recorded in the item/design doc.
2. Each give-away game unlocks when the player achieves its configured trigger achievements: **"win your first game" plus one additional achievement** (suggested: first win in a second distinct game — final choice recorded, see Appendix). Trigger definitions live in one config (achievement ids → game id) and are game-agnostic.
3. The unlock uses **the same mechanism as the follow-on-Steam free game** (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC): bundled content, locked by default, unlocked in place, persisted across launches, game-agnostic unlock logic.
4. Unlock state persists across launches; re-checks on demand; graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent (CTA/lock state degrades without crashing the app).
5. Trigger achievements come from the engine-generic achievement layer (CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ): give-away config consumes achievement-unlock events, not game-specific hacks.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Reuse, don't reinvent:** the unlock mechanism (bundled-content unlock, persistence, game-agnostic design) is the one designed in CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC; this item adds achievement-triggered unlocks as an additional trigger source on the same path.
- **Game selection is a business decision** and part of this item's scope (user: "don't know yet (note Main Street)").
- **Dependencies:** blocked by CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ (achievements exist as engine-generic events) and CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC (unlock mechanism). Both are prerequisites for implementation.
- **Trigger achievements:** "win your first game" plus one more (user decision; second achievement suggested — final choice to be confirmed).
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).

## Existing state

- Follow-on-Steam item (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC, intake_complete) designs the game-agnostic free-game unlock: Steamworks-based follow detection + local unlock persistence + bundled DLC content; **not yet implemented** — this item should coordinate so the unlock path is shared.
- No achievement system exists yet; CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ (challenges → Steam achievements, engine-generic) is the event source this item consumes.
- Game catalog (`main.ts` GAMES): Gym (demos), 9-Card Golf, Beleaguered Castle, Sushi Go!, Feudalism, Lost Cities, Main Street, Blackjack, Coloretto. Steam launcher (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) will bundle a subset with DLC architecture.
- CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC has an open question: which game is the designated free follow-bonus (business decision, game-agnostic ACs) — give-away selection must not conflict with it.

## Desired change

1. **Select and document the three give-away games** (business decision; Main Street noted as a candidate; rationale recorded).
2. Define the **trigger config** (achievement ids from CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ's manifest → unlocked game id) in one place (e.g. `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts`).
3. **Extend the shared unlock mechanism** from CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC to accept achievement-triggered unlocks (same persistence/unlock path; new trigger source alongside the follow trigger).
4. **UI:** locked give-away games shown in the Game Selector with unlock progress (which trigger achievements remain); unlocked games become playable.
5. Tests (mocked trigger source + unlock persistence; headless unit tests) + documentation.

## Key Files

- `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts` (new) — give-away config: trigger achievement ids → game id; selection rationale comment.
- `electron/` unlock module from CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC — extended with the achievement trigger source (shared path, game-agnostic).
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` (or launcher UI module) — locked state + unlock progress display for give-away games.
- Achievement manifest from CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ — the trigger ids referenced by the config.
- `tests/` — unit tests for trigger evaluation and unlock persistence with mocked sources.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md` — give-away configuration and QA workflow documentation.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC – Follow-on-Steam incentive: unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher** (open, intake_complete) — the unlock mechanism this item reuses; its open question on the follow-bonus game choice must be coordinated with give-away selection.
- **CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ – Challenges as achievements: sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements** (open, idea) — the engine-generic achievement event source; blocked-by for this item.
- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, plan_complete) — the Steam version hosting both features.
- `main.ts` GAMES catalog — the candidate pool for the three give-away games.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ and CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC land first; this item's implementation is gated on both.
- **Assumption:** The three give-away games are chosen from the current catalog; Main Street is a candidate (user note).
- **Risk:** Conflict between the follow-on-Steam bonus game and the give-away set (e.g. same game twice, or devaluing the follow incentive) — mitigation: selection and rationale recorded, coordinated with the follow-item's open question.
- **Risk:** If the achievement layer (CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ) is delayed, the trigger source is missing — mitigation: define the trigger config/interface in this item early, independent of Steam sync internals.
- **Scope-creep risk:** trading cards, seasonal give-aways, paid DLC sales, and anti-abuse (achievement-farm detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Do you already have the three games in mind, or should the work item include evaluating/selecting them from the catalog (e.g. Main Street, Golf, Blackjack…)?"
  — Answer (user): "don't know yet (note Main Street)". Source: interactive reply (2026-08-09). Implication: selection is a deliverable of this item; Main Street is a recorded candidate.
- Q2: "Should the give-away unlock on specific milestone achievements (e.g. 'complete all challenges in a game', 'win your first game'), or on any achievement being reached?"

Source: interactive reply (2026-08-09). **Suggested second achievement: "win your first game in a second distinct game"** (rewards breadth of play; both triggers are engine-generic and achievable without the give-away game itself). Alternative candidates: "complete your first full game" (reach a game-over screen without quitting) or "complete all challenges in any game". Final choice to be confirmed at planning.

# Intake Brief: Implement Community Favour mechanic (CG-0MSTOATDQ005XDET)

## Problem statement

Main Street gives players a single action per turn (buy/move/place) plus a Hint and End Turn. When a player cannot afford any market purchase, the turn offers no meaningful decision — they simply pass. The Community Favour mechanic adds a once-per-turn resource exchange (coins ↔ reputation) available every MarketPhase, giving players a fallback action and creating a "save for a business vs invest in reputation" tension.

## Users

- **New players** (tutorial): learn that reputation is a spendable resource that can be converted to coins when short on cash.
- **Regular players**: use Community Favour to smooth early-game resource imbalance (coin-rich/reputation-poor and vice versa) and to keep turns meaningful when no purchase is affordable.
- **AI players**: gain a legal fallback action so AI turns never stall on an unaffordable market.

Example user story: "As a player who can't afford the market card I want, I can spend reputation to gain coins so I don't waste my turn."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Engine action:** A new `PlayerAction` of type `community-favour` with a `direction` (`'coins-to-rep' | 'rep-to-coins'`) is implemented in `executeAction`, validated by the EconomyLedger, and legal only during `MarketPhase`, at most **once per turn** (enforced by a `favourUsedThisTurn` flag reset at `DayStart`).
- **AC2 — Exchange rates:** Defaults follow the brainstorming notes and are tunable per-difficulty via `GameConfig`: **2 coins → 1 reputation**; **2 reputation → 3 coins**. Round-trip is lossy (2 coins → 1 rep → 1.5 coins) so no infinite arbitrage is possible. (Producer delegated balancing; rates live in config constants like `reputationCoinDivisor`.)
- **AC3 — UI:** Two separate buttons in the market-phase action bar (one per direction), rendered via SLL zones in `main-street.layout.json`. Buttons are disabled when the player lacks the required resource, when `favourUsedThisTurn` is true, or outside `MarketPhase`. Interaction follows the established animated/sounded action pattern (popTextOrIcon + `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` SFX).
- **AC4 — Tutorial:** The tutorial teaches the mechanic with a new action-gated step inserted between T12 and T13 (renumbered T13–T17 → T14–T18), requiring the player to perform the rep→coins direction to afford the Library ($7). Tutorial scenario starting coins reduced from **16 → 12** so the conversion is required (budget: 12 − 4 + 0.625 − 3 + 1.25 = 6.875 < 7 → must convert 2 rep → 3 coins). `TutorialActionType` gains a `community-favour` value wired into `isTutorialActionAllowed` / `isRequiredAction`. - **AC5 — AI:** `enumerateLegalActions` includes the `community-favour` action when affordable and unused; `scoreAction` assigns a sensible heuristic score; AI turns use the same animated/sounded path as human turns.

- **AC7 — Tests:** Unit tests cover: legal exchange, both directions, insufficient funds rejection, once-per-turn enforcement + DayStart reset, MarketPhase gating, legacy save backfill, AI enumeration/scoring. Browser test covers both buttons rendering, disabling, and a full exchange round. All related docs (see Key Files) are updated, and the full project test suite (`npm test`) plus `npm run build` pass.

## Existing state

- `PlayerAction` union (`MainStreetEngine.ts`) has no exchange action; `executeAction` decrements `actionsRemaining` for purchase actions.

## Desired change

Add the Community Favour exchange to the engine, UI, AI, tutorial, persistence, and transcripts, with per-difficulty configurable rates and a once-per-turn guard. Reduce the tutorial scenario's starting coins so the Library step requires a rep→coins conversion, demonstrating the mechanic's liquidity value.

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Add `CommunityFavourAction` to `PlayerAction`, new `case 'community-favour'` in `executeAction`, validation (MarketPhase, once-per-turn, ledger check), `DayStart` flag reset.

- `example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json` — Add SLL zones/anchors for the favour buttons.

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Add the action to `enumerateLegalActions` and `scoreAction`.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — Insert the new action-gated step between T12/T13; renumber T13–T17 → T14–T18; extend `TutorialActionType`.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialScenario.ts` — Reduce starting coins 16 → 12; update the coin-budget doc table.
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — Tutorial copy for the new step.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetTranscript.ts` — Ensure the action is captured (existing `'action'` event covers it; add descriptor typing if needed).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Verify AI games remain valid with the new action; regenerate affected baseline fixtures if AI behavior shifts.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Baseline churn:** Adding a legal AI action changes AI decision ordering → Monte Carlo CSVs and catalog baselines may shift; baselines must be regenerated via the existing `generate-*-baseline` scripts (verified locally before push).
- **Tutorial budget tightness:** Reducing starting coins to 12 makes the tutorial budget tight by design (the festival at T14 offsets the Library spend); the budget table and T12/T13 copy must be updated consistently. - **Renumbering risk:** Inserting a step renumbers T13–T17 → T14–T18; all references (i18n keys, E2E tests, `tutorial-en.ts`, `TutorialFlow.ts` docs) must be updated in the same change.
- **Scope guard:** No changes to card data, street grid, adjacency, or challenge systems; the exchange is purely a resource operation. Any ideas discovered during implementation (e.g. a market "sell card for coins" mechanic) should be filed as new work items, not folded in.
- **Assumption (documented):** The action does **not** consume `actionsRemaining` — it is a free once-per-turn action available during MarketPhase, so it functions as a true fallback when the player cannot afford a purchase. This preserves the description's intent ("meaningful action every turn, even when they cannot afford a market purchase") and avoids competing with the purchase economy. Are these rates confirmed, or should they be balanced differently (e.g. asymmetric 3:1/4:1)?" — Answer (Producer, interactive reply): "balance them as you see fit". Final decision: keep 2→1 and 2→3 as defaults, exposed as per-difficulty config constants; round-trip is lossy (25% haircut on the rep→coins leg) which prevents arbitrage. Research: reviewed `MainStreetDifficulty.ts` (reputationCoinDivisor/maxReputationCoinMultiplier pattern) and `MainStreetState.ts` (EconomyLedger sync) — rates are purely data-level, no engine changes needed to retune later.

# Intake Brief: Business cards incur ongoing per-turn cost (1/4 purchase price, min 0.25), even in hand

**Headline:** Every business card in Main Street gains an `ongoingCost` field (set per-card in CSV) that is deducted from coins every turn during the income phase — whether the card is placed on the street grid or held in the player's hand.

## Problem statement

Main Street already applies ongoing costs to staff cards and community-space cards (Library) each income phase. Business cards — the core tableau cards players invest in — currently have no running cost, making them pure income generators once placed. Adding an ongoing cost for business cards creates a meaningful trade-off: placing a business card is a capital investment that also commits recurring funds.

## Users

- **Players** building a Main Street tableau: business cards now have a running cost that affects long-term strategy — higher-cost cards are riskier to hold and place.
- **Producer/balance analysts**: the ongoing cost field (CSV) feeds the balance methodology, just like `ongoingCost` on staff and community-space cards.

User stories:
- "As a player, I want to see the per-turn cost of each business card displayed on the card art and in tooltips, so I can factor ongoing expenses into my placement decisions."
- "As a player, I want business cards I hold in hand to still incur their per-turn cost, so that hoarding expensive cards is penalised."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **BusinessCard interface:** The `BusinessCard` interface in `MainStreetCards.ts` gains a `readonly ongoingCost: number` property (defaults to `0` for legacy cards).
2. **CSV parsing:** `parseBusinessRow` / `makeBusiness` reads the existing `ongoingCost` CSV column (column 28) and assigns it to the `BusinessCard` instance. Cards with missing/empty `ongoingCost` default to `0`.
3. **Per-turn deduction:** A new `applyBusinessOngoingCosts(state)` function iterates over **all business cards in `state.hand` AND all business cards on `state.streetGrid`**, sums their `ongoingCost` values, and deducts the total from `coins` during the income phase. Deduction is clamped at 0 coins (no negative coins) and logged to the activity log with the same pattern as `applyStaffOngoingCosts` / `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts`.
4. **Turn integration:** `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` is called in `processEndOfTurn` during the `IncomePhase`, immediately after `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts`.
5. **Visual display:** Business card SVG generation (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) and tooltip formatting (`cardTooltipText`) show the ongoing cost when > 0, using the same `-[value]/turn` format as staff/community-space cards (red/orange text).
6. **Card display:** Cards in hand and on the street grid display the ongoing cost visually (SVG-based card art shows `-0.50/turn` style label).
7. **Testing:** Unit tests validate that: (a) `ongoingCost` is parsed from CSV for business cards; (b) `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` deducts from both hand and street cards; (c) coins are clamped at 0; (d) the cost appears in card SVG and tooltip; (e) `processEndOfTurn` correctly chains the new function.

## Constraints

- The `ongoingCost` CSV column already exists (column 28) — no CSV schema change needed. The column is currently populated only for staff/community-space cards; business cards have an empty trailing value.
- Deduction happens **every turn** during the income phase — no separate "round" concept.
- Only the `business` card family is affected (not `community-space`, `staff`, `event`, or `upgrade`).
- Existing save data with business cards will serialize correctly (the field is `readonly` but set at parse time; legacy deserialised cards get default `0`).
- The min 0.25 is a balance decision for individual card data, not a code-level clamp — the engine deducts whatever value is on the card.

## Existing state

- `BusinessCard` interface (`MainStreetCards.ts` lines ~232–310): no `ongoingCost` property.
- `StaffCard` interface (`MainStreetCards.ts` lines ~394–400): has `readonly ongoingCost: number`.
- `CommunitySpaceCard` interface (`MainStreetCards.ts` lines ~954–961): has `readonly ongoingCost: number`.
- `parseBusinessRow` (`MainStreetCards.ts` line ~99): does NOT read `ongoingCost` from CSV.
- `parseStaffRow` / `parseCommunitySpaceRow`: DO read `ongoingCost`.
- `processEndOfTurn` (`MainStreetEngine.ts` line ~782): calls `applyIncome`, `applyStaffOngoingCosts`, `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts`.
- `applyStaffOngoingCosts` / `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts` (`MainStreetEngine.ts` lines ~1217–1270): deduct costs, clamp at 0, log.
- SVG generation (`MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` `generateBusinessCardSvg`): does NOT show ongoing cost for business cards (only for staff/community-space in other functions).
- Tooltip formatting (`MainStreetFormatting.ts` `cardTooltipText`): does NOT show `ongoingCost` for business cards.

## Desired change

1. Add `ongoingCost` to the `BusinessCard` interface.
2. Wire `ongoingCost` into `parseBusinessRow` / `makeBusiness` (read from CSV column 28).
3. Create `applyBusinessOngoingCosts(state)` following the `applyStaffOngoingCosts` pattern, iterating over both hand and street.
4. Call `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` in `processEndOfTurn` during income phase.
5. Update `generateBusinessCardSvg` to render ongoing cost label (red text, "-X/turn" below cost circle).
6. Update `cardTooltipText` for `business` family to include ongoing cost info.
7. Add unit tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Add `ongoingCost` to `BusinessCard` interface; wire into `parseBusinessRow` / `makeBusiness`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Add `applyBusinessOngoingCosts()`; call it in `processEndOfTurn`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — Update `cardTooltipText` for business family to show ongoing cost.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — Update `generateBusinessCardSvg` to render ongoing cost label.
- `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` (new) — Unit tests for the new mechanic.
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Populate `ongoingCost` column for business cards (balance: 1/4 purchase price, min 0.25).

## Related work

- **CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE** "Why would a library bring in money" — Introduced `ongoingCost` for community-space cards; established the pattern for `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts`.
- **CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX** "Staff job-applicant specialization mechanic" — Staff cards already have `ongoingCost`; the pattern for `applyStaffOngoingCosts` is the canonical reference.
- **CG-0MSXUHPGT003ZMU2** "Browser test: assert count-only rendering in game-over overlay" (find-related hit — tangential, no direct impact).
- **CG-0MS7UEUL000610A2** "When buying a card it animates to the wrong position" (find-related hit — tangential, no direct impact).
- **CG-0MQGJXW67008DZ39** "Coloretto full rules expansion" (find-related hit — tangential, no direct impact).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Legacy save data:** Deserialised `BusinessCard` objects from older saves won't have `ongoingCost` (will be `undefined`). Mitigation: `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` uses `card.ongoingCost ?? 0` (nullish coalescing), consistent with existing ongoing-cost functions.
- **CSV data entry:** The seed mentions "1/4 purchase price, min 0.25" — documented as a balance decision for CSV data entry, NOT a code-level clamp. All ~50 business cards need manual CSV population by a producer; engine implementation is independent.
- **Scope creep — other families:** Only the `business` family is affected. `upgrade`, `event`, `staff`, and `community-space` cards are excluded. The per-card field structure already supports future extension.
- **Hand holding:** Players can hold up to 3 business cards in hand (CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2). Cumulative hand + street ongoing costs could be significant; this is a balance concern, not an implementation risk.
- **Docs:** `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (Ongoing Cost table, income-phase summary) and `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` must be updated per the doc-update policy.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Per-card field vs. computed formula: for business cards, should each card have its own `ongoingCost` in CSV, or should it be a computed value `Math.max(0.25, cost / 4)` from the purchase price?" — Answer (producer): "In CSV". Research: the CSV already has an `ongoingCost` column (column 28) used by staff and community-space card rows; business rows currently leave it empty. The seed's "1/4 purchase price, min 0.25" is a balance guideline for populating that CSV column, not engine logic. Source: interactive reply during intake.
- Q2: "'End of the round' vs. Main Street's turn model: Main Street operates on turns, not rounds. Does 'deducted at the end of the round' mean every turn during the income phase?" — Answer (producer): "every turn". Research: `processEndOfTurn` (`MainStreetEngine.ts`) runs an `IncomePhase` each turn and already calls `applyStaffOngoingCosts` and `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts` there; the new business cost hooks into the same phase. Source: interactive reply during intake; `MainStreetEngine.ts:782`.
- Q3: "Scope of 'business cards': Main Street has business, community-space, staff, event, and upgrade families. Does 'all business cards' mean only the `business` family?" — Answer (producer): "only business". Research: `BusinessCard` is the core tableau-card family (`MainStreetCards.ts:232`); it currently lacks `ongoingCost`, unlike `StaffCard` and `CommunitySpaceCard`. The mechanic excludes upgrades, events, staff, and community spaces. Source: interactive reply during intake.

# Intake Brief: Graffiti Art — reputation only (no coins)

## Problem statement

The Graffiti Art good-incident card (`evt-graffiti-art`) in Main Street currently grants **+1 coin to all businesses AND +1 reputation**. It should grant reputation only (+0 coins, +1 reputation), matching the design intent of reputation-focused positive incidents (parallel to the Free Health Screening card change in CG-0MSXIS2QI002WMKR).

## Users / context

- Main Street players encounter incident events that modify resources. Some incidents give coins, some give reputation, and some give both.
- Graffiti Art is a "good" polarity, tier-3, universal ("All") incident. Its theme ("artists transform the street with murals") is a community/cultural initiative — fitting for reputation gains, not coin generation.
- Graffiti Art is the exact mirror of the "Graffiti" bad incident (`evt-graffiti`), which gives -1/-1 to all businesses.

1. **Graffiti Art grants reputation only** — `coinDelta` changed from `1` to `0` in `card-data.csv`; the event resolves to +0 coins and +1 reputation to all businesses.

5. **Full project test suite passes** — all unit tests, browser tests, and E2E tutorials pass with no regressions.

## Constraints

- This is a single-card behavior change — scope is limited to `evt-graffiti-art`.

## Desired change

## Key Files (predicted)

Document this design decision. |

## Related work

- **CG-0MSXIS2QI002WMKR** — "Main Street: Free Health Screening grants reputation only (no coins)" — parallel change, completed, same pattern (coinDelta 1→0).
- **CG-0MSRC9UR9006FBXC** — "Main Street: add Graffiti Art good-incident card" — original creation of evt-graffiti-art with coinDelta=1.

- *Q: Does the net polarity change (+2 → +1) affect the incident-polarity balance constraint?* — **Answer:** Net delta is still > 0, so it remains classified as "good" polarity. The balance constraint (good/bad/neutral count) is preserved.

# Replace incident deck pre-ordering with runtime balanced card selection

## Problem Statement

The current incident deck uses `orderIncidentDeck()` to pre-order the entire face-down deck at build/reshuffle time using a soft-greedy algorithm. While this strongly favours repeat-spacing and streak constraints across the deck body, it can admit rare tail deviations when the pool is imbalanced, and the pre-arranged order changes the deterministic simulation in ways that are harder to predict and test (monte-carlo median widened from ~39.8 to ~153).

The fix: instead of pre-ordering, select each incident card **at runtime** from the remaining face-down deck pool, constrained by the resolved draw history. The deck remains face-down; only the selection mechanism changes.

## Users

- **Player (Main Street)**: Experiences fair, balanced incidents without visible deck manipulation — no card order visible, only the resolved sequence matters.
- **Developer/Tester**: Can reproduce deterministic game outcomes (same seed → same result) and reason about incident balance without tracking pre-order algorithms.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Runtime selection**: `resolveIncident()` selects the next incident card at runtime from the remaining face-down pool using constraint-aware selection (`repeatSpacing` / `maxStreak`), instead of popping from a pre-ordered sequence. The deck is shuffled once at setup/reshuffle; cards are removed by index.
2. **Determinism preserved**: Same game seed produces the same incident draw sequence. The selection is fully deterministic (no RNG consumed during selection — constraints are evaluated against the pool order).
3. **Constraint compliance**: The same repeat-spacing (N) and max-streak (M) constraints from `IncidentBalanceState` are enforced at draw time using the existing tiered constraint relaxation (strict → relax-repeat → invariant-window → invariant-any → fallback).
4. **Reshuffle integration**: `replenishIncidentDeck()` shuffles remaining incident cards from the event deck/discards and then uses runtime selection (not pre-ordering) for subsequent draws.
5. **Full test suite passes**: Existing incident-balance tests are updated to reflect runtime selection; all Monte Carlo guardrails and regression tests pass.
6. **Documentation updated**: Code comments and docs (DEVELOPER.md incident-balance sections) reflect the runtime-selection mechanism, replacing pre-ordering references.

## Constraints

- Must keep seeded determinism — same seed produces the same draw sequence.
- Selection must consume no RNG (constraint evaluation is deterministic against deck order).
- Deck remains face-down and invisible to the player (UI unchanged).
- Backward compatibility with saved games must be maintained (existing saves use pre-ordered decks; deserialization should handle both formats).
- The existing `IncidentBalanceState` and `recordIncidentDraw()` must continue to work unchanged.

## Existing State

- **`MainStreetCards.ts`**: Contains `orderIncidentDeck()` (pre-orders entire pool) and `findConstrainedIncidentIndex()` (runtime selection from a deck). Both use the same constraint tier system.
- **`MainStreetMarket.ts`**: `replenishIncidentDeck()` calls `orderIncidentDeck()` at reshuffle time.
- **`MainStreetState.ts`**: `setupMainStreetGame()` calls `orderIncidentDeck()` at game start.
- **`MainStreetEngine.ts`**: `resolveIncident()` pops `incidentDeck.shift()` (pre-ordered card at front).
- **`tests/main-street/incident-balance.test.ts`**: Tests the current pre-order system via `orderIncidentDeck`.

## Desired Change

Replace `orderIncidentDeck()` with runtime selection using `findConstrainedIncidentIndex()` (or a refined variant). The flow becomes:

1. **Setup/reshuffle**: Gather incident pool → shuffle (seeded) → store as `incidentDeck`.
2. **Draw**: Call `findConstrainedIncidentIndex(deck, balance)` → remove chosen card by index → record draw with `recordIncidentDraw()`.

`findConstrainedIncidentIndex` already exists and implements the exact constraint logic needed. The change is to use it at draw time instead of pre-ordering.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Remove or deprecate `orderIncidentDeck`; `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` already exists
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — Update `replenishIncidentDeck()` to shuffle-only (no `orderIncidentDeck`)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Update `setupMainStreetGame()` to shuffle-only for incident pool
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Update `resolveIncident()` to use runtime selection instead of `shift()`
- `tests/main-street/incident-balance.test.ts` — Update tests to reflect runtime selection; verify determinism

## Related Work

- **CG-0MSXOVQFL007G3VH** — Implement constraint-aware deck ordering (the pre-ordering system being replaced)
- **CG-0MSL0OP040043KKZ** — Incident Balance state (IncidentBalanceState, recordIncidentDraw, findConstrainedIncidentIndex)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: Performance** — `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` scans the full deck each draw (O(N)). With ~60-80 incident cards, this is negligible.
- **Risk: Saved games** — Pre-ordered decks in legacy saves are treated as initial state; subsequent draws use runtime selection. Balance history drives constraints, not deck order.
- **Assumption:** `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` constraint logic is sufficient without modification. If the tier system needs refinement, that is tracked separately.
- **Scope guard:** This task replaces pre-ordering with runtime selection only. No changes to constraint thresholds, difficulty presets, or UI.
- **Opportunity (out of scope):** If runtime selection reveals new balancing insights, a follow-up task can tune `incidentRepeatSpacing` / `incidentMaxStreak` presets.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q**: Should we deprecate `orderIncidentDeck()` or keep it for legacy compatibility? — **Answer (Map)**: Deprecate and remove. The runtime selection approach fully replaces it. Any legacy code paths that reference it are internal and not exposed.
- **Q**: Does `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` need any modifications for runtime selection? — **Answer (Map)**: `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` already returns the array index of the chosen card and works against a deck in the expected format. No modifications needed — it already implements the constraint tiers exactly as required.
- **Q**: How should saved games (which contain pre-ordered decks) be handled? — **Answer (Map)**: Saved game deserialization already handles the `incidentDeck → incidentBalance` migration. Pre-ordered decks in saves are treated as initial state; subsequent draws use runtime selection. No special handling needed — the balance history is the source of truth for constraints, not deck order.
data.risk: Low — findConstrainedIncidentIndex already implements the needed constraint logic; only wiring changes. Determinism preserved.

The staff applicant mechanic (CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX) needs a rich pool of new staff-member applicant cards and specialization skills beyond the existing 9 templates (all hand-slot focused) and the minimum "Town Gossip" skill. This provides players with meaningful choices when applicants arrive, varied gameplay identities, and strategic depth in building a specialized team.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants diverse applicant cards with distinct gameplay identities and specialization skills that create meaningful hiring decisions and long-term strategic advantages.
- **Game designer** — wants a modular, balanced skill pool that synergizes with existing business types and synergy families, and can be extended without breaking the mechanic.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **10+ new staff card templates** proposed with distinct gameplay identities, CSV-ready data (id, name, description, tier, ongoingCost), and clear thematic fit for Main Street's business ecosystem.
2. **10+ specialization skills** proposed with defined mechanical effects, balanced impact ranges, and clear synergies with existing synergy types (Food, Culture, Commerce, Service, Entertainment, Health).

4. **Skill-effect categories** — Skills are organized into effect categories (income boost, reputation boost, cost reduction, incident mitigation, synergy enhancement) with balanced impact ranges documented per category. # Main Street: Upcoming panel — replace face-down deck card with compact deck counter

## Problem statement

The Upcoming/incident panel dedicates ~70px to a face-down card-back image plus ~12px for deck-count text, leaving insufficient vertical space for the duration-effect text lines that the income-phase animation (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ) needs to display per-affected business card.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player (income-phase visibility):** "When my turn's income resolves, I want to see the duration-effect text lines for upcoming cards without the panel overflowing or the active-effect lines disappearing."
- **Player (reduced motion):** "I want the panel layout to remain readable without animation — the deck counter should be clearly visible and the effect text should be legible."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The face-down card-back image in the Upcoming panel is replaced by a compact deck counter (rounded rectangle with card icon and count number) that fits within ~24px of vertical space.
2. The panel height shrinks by at least 50px (the ~70px card-back + ~12px text, minus the ~24px counter), making that space available for income-phase duration-effect text lines.
3. The deck counter updates reactively whenever `state.incidentDeck.length` changes (e.g., cards drawn, deck reshuffled).
4. The deck counter's click/tap area (if any) preserves existing tooltip behaviour — clicking the counter shows the remaining deck count, or the panel has no interactive elements (no-click, pass-through).
5. Reduced-motion mode renders the deck counter without animation; the visual design is identical to full-motion (no animation = no layout difference).
6. All unit + browser tests pass: layout geometry tests (panel height, card-center calculation compatibility with `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()`), deck counter render/update, and the income-phase dependency (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ).

## Constraints

- **Panel width unchanged:** Only vertical space is affected.
- **`getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` compatibility:** The incident-reveal flight and staff-peek reveal (CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6 / CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN) use this method to get the card center for animation origins. If the counter changes the vertical centering math, update the method to return the same logical origin (the position where the face-down deck would have been centred).
- **SLL layout binding:** The panel height is driven by the SLL layout (`MAIN_STREET_SLL_LAYOUT` zone `incidentQueue`). If the SLL zone has a fixed height, either: (a) the zone height is already a max-height / min-height constraint (preferred), or (b) the deck counter is placed within the existing zone with overflow clipped (documented limitation).
- **No new SFX keys.** The deck counter is a static/non-interactive element — no sound effects.
- **Re-use existing SVG rasterisation:** If the card icon needs to be an SVG, use `SvgHelpers` / `makeTextureKey()` pattern from `GymSvgHelpersScene`.
- **Headless/replay exemption:** No rendering changes visible in headless/replay modes.

## Existing state

- `refreshIncidentQueue()` in `MainStreetRenderer.ts` renders: title bar (22px) → face-down card-back (~69px) → deck count text (~12px) → active-effect lines (16px × N + 16px overhead) → bottom padding (8px).
- `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` returns the logical center of the face-down card for animation purposes.
- Constants: `BASE_QUEUE_CARD_W = 120`, `BASE_QUEUE_CARD_H = 69`.
- Parent work item (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ) adds income-phase duration-effect lines to the panel.

## Desired change

1. **Remove** the face-down card-back SVG render and the separate deck-count text label from `refreshIncidentQueue()`.
2. **Add** a compact deck counter: a small rounded rectangle (~100px wide × 20px tall) containing a small card-icon (12×12px) on the left and the count number (e.g., "Deck: 5") in 10px text on the right.
3. **Update** `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` if the counter's vertical centre differs from the old card-back centre; ensure incident-reveal animations still target the correct origin.
4. **Ensure** the panel's dynamic height calculation accounts for the new counter's reduced height.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `refreshIncidentQueue()` (deck counter replacement), `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` (origin math)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — constants (if new counter dimensions need constants)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` — SLL zone height binding (if the incidentQueue zone needs adjustment)

## Related work

- **CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ** "Income Phase: phased card-effect animations" (blocked-by this item) — needs the freed panel space for duration-effect text lines.
- **CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6** / **CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN** — incident-reveal flight and staff-peek reveal; must remain compatible with `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` after deck counter changes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **SLL zone height rigidity:** If the `incidentQueue` SLL zone has a fixed pixel height, reducing the panel's internal content won't shrink the zone itself — the extra space may be unused. Mitigation: inspect SLL zone height type; if fixed, the zone height can be left as-is (no regression), or adjusted if it's a max-height constraint.
- **`getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` origin shift:** Removing the ~69px card-back and replacing it with a ~20px counter shifts the visual centre. Mitigation: keep the counter centred at the same Y origin as the old card-back, so animation targets are unchanged.
- **Scope creep:** This is a pure visual/layout change. Do not include: changing incident-draw logic, changing active-effect display, adding new interaction patterns, or modifying the incident deck draw animation.

## Goal
Teach the Community Favour mechanic by inserting a new action-gated step between T12 and T13, renumbering the following steps, and reducing the tutorial starting coins so the rep→coins conversion is required to afford the Library.

- **AC1 — New TutorialActionType:** `TutorialActionType` in `TutorialFlow.ts` gains a `'community-favour'` value, wired into `isTutorialActionAllowed` and `isRequiredAction` so the step is action-gated.

- **AC2 — New step:** A new action-gated step is inserted between T12 and T13 (before the Library purchase) that requires the player to perform the `rep-to-coins` direction of Community Favour (2 rep → 3 coins) so they can afford the Library.

- **AC3 — Renumber:** T13–T17 are renumbered to T14–T18. All references updated in the same change: `TutorialFlow.ts` step IDs, `i18n/tutorial-en.ts` keys, E2E tests, and any doc references.

- **AC6 — i18n copy:** New i18n key(s) added for the inserted step title/body in `tutorial-en.ts`.

# Activity log no longer scrolls

## Problem statement

The Main Street activity log no longer auto-scrolls to show the latest content. New log entries (income, incident results, purchases, staff costs, etc.) accumulate off-screen at the bottom of the panel while the view stays pinned at the top showing the earliest entries, so the player cannot see the most recent game events without manually wheel-scrolling.

## Users

- **Main Street players** — rely on the activity log to see the latest game events (turn headers, income, incident results, purchase/pay effects, win/loss).
- **Tutorial/review users** — use the log to verify that their actions took effect.

### User stories

- "As a player, when I buy a card or an incident resolves, I want the log to scroll so I can see the new entry without manual scrolling."
- "As a player, when I scroll up to re-read an older entry, I don't want the log to yank me back down on the next event."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When new log entries are added while the player is at (or near) the bottom of the log, the log auto-scrolls so the newest entry is visible.
2. When the player has scrolled up to read history, adding a new entry must NOT steal their scroll position (auto-scroll stays paused until they return to the bottom).
3. When the player wheel-scrolls back to the bottom, auto-scroll re-engages for subsequent entries.
4. On scene restart / new game, the log renders correctly with no content scrolled off the top of the panel (no regression of CG-0MR4XUJM9008GK6Z).
5. Behavior is covered by automated tests (unit/browser): the existing browser tests that codify the current non-auto-scrolling behaviour are updated to assert the restored auto-scroll behaviour.
6. Full project test suite (`npm test`) and production build (`npm run build`) pass with the changes.
7. Relevant documentation (code comments in `refreshLog`/`handleLogWheel`, and any activity-log guidance in `docs/`) is updated to reflect the restored behaviour.

## Constraints

- Preserve the "don't yank the reader" UX: auto-scroll must engage only when the user is at/near the bottom (existing `logAutoScroll` mechanism — do not replace it).
- Preserve the scene-restart safety fix from CG-0MR4XUJM9008GK6Z (stale scroll state must not hide all entries on restart).
- Main Street only; no engine/other-game impact expected.

## Existing state

- `logAutoScroll` starts `false` (MainStreetScene.ts line 117, reset in MainStreetLifecycleManager.create ~line 185).
- `refreshLog()` (MainStreetRenderer.ts ~line 1627): on overflow, keeps `logScrollOffset` clamped at its current value when `logAutoScroll` is false, then sets `logAutoScroll = (logScrollOffset >= logMaxScroll - 4)`. Because the offset starts at 0 (top) and content overflows by more than 4px, `atBottom` is false → `logAutoScroll` stays false forever; the log never moves until the user wheel-scrolls to the bottom (which re-engages it via `handleLogWheel`).
- Browser tests codify this behaviour: `tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` ("does not position content above the log display area when entries first overflow" asserts `logAutoScroll === false` and offset stays 0; "auto-scroll snaps to bottom..." manually sets `logAutoScroll = true`, masking the real flow).

## Root cause (regression)

Commit `0b642a6e` — CG-0MR4XUJM9008GK6Z ("Fix initial logAutoScroll to false to prevent content scrolling off the top") changed the initial `logAutoScroll` from `true` to `false` in both `MainStreetScene.ts` and `MainStreetLifecycleManager.create()`. Its stated assumption — "auto-scroll kicks in naturally when the user scrolls to the bottom" — is wrong for the default flow: the `atBottom` re-enable check in `refreshLog` never becomes true while the offset stays pinned at the top, so auto-scroll never engages. History: `git log -S "logAutoScroll = true"` → the original was `true` (0bd7eaf6), so this is a behavioural regression.

## Desired change

Restore "start at the bottom (latest entries) and auto-scroll on new entries unless the user has scrolled up":

- Set the initial `logAutoScroll` back to `true` (class property + create() reset), **and** ensure the scene-restart case still clamps correctly (the existing `Phaser.Math.Clamp` branch already guards stale offsets; worst case a restart resets offsets to 0 with an empty/new log so maxScroll recomputes to 0 — safe).
- Keep `handleLogWheel`'s re-engage-on-bottom logic unchanged.
- Update the browser tests that assert the current non-scrolling behaviour, and add a regression test that reproduces the real flow (fresh scene → entries accumulate → offset reaches bottom / latest visible without manual scroll), plus a test for "scrolled up → new entry does not yank position".
- Sanity-check the mask/visibility safety net still renders correctly at the bottom.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `logAutoScroll` property initial value (line 117).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts` — scene-create reset of `logAutoScroll` (~line 185).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `refreshLog()` scroll bounds/auto-scroll logic (~lines 1627–1720).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetInputManager.ts` — `handleLogWheel` bottom re-engage threshold (reference, likely unchanged).
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` — update tests codifying current behaviour; add regression tests.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — restart test asserts container `y > 0`; verify still valid after the change.

## Related work

- **CG-0MR4XUJM9008GK6Z** — "Activity log extends beyond the bottom of the content area" (completed) — the commit (`0b642a6e`) that introduced this regression; its acceptance criteria include the restart-safety requirement that must not regress.
- **CG-0MSRGVGU40044GJ0** — "Undo/redo feedback notification" (completed) — logged as related by `/skill:find-related`; UI feedback adjacent, no functional dependency.
- **CG-0MSLXJCHH001DLIO** / **CG-0MSAZL6O2008PTWY** — surfaced by `/skill:find-related` (score-threshold noise; not functionally related to log scrolling).
- Original scroll implementation precedent (git ref, not a worklog item): commit `0bd7eaf6` (CG-0MM8MZ8IK0TCYV79 "Add activity log with state tracking, engine instrumentation, UI panel, and tests") — initial `logAutoScroll = true`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "scrolls to show the latest content" means the log default view is the bottom (newest entries), with auto-scroll on new entries while the user is at the bottom — i.e. restoring the pre-0b642a6e UX. This matches the bug title ("no longer scrolls") and standard log-panel convention.
- **Assumption:** current priority `medium` is appropriate (non-blocking, user-facing UX regression); may be re-considered to `high` if gameplay clarity is deemed significant by the producer.
- **Risk (scope creep):** restoring `logAutoScroll = true` may re-expose the original "content off the top" restart symptom if clamping is insufficient — mitigate with the existing clamp + explicit restart coverage, not by rebuilding the scroll system.
- **Risk:** other tests may implicitly depend on the log starting at the top (e.g. `MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` restart test asserting `logContentContainer.y > 0`); verify and adjust assertions rather than behaviour.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the log default to showing the latest entries (bottom) — i.e. restore the pre-regression behaviour — as implied by the report?" — Answer: **Not asked; assumed yes (documented above).** The bug title ("used to scroll to show the latest content … no longer automatically does so") states the expected behaviour directly, and the pre-regression implementation (`logAutoScroll = true`) matches it. Source: work item CG-0MT24HFNM002MPF5 description + git archaeology (commit `0b642a6e` vs `0bd7eaf6`).
- Q: "Should auto-scroll pause while the user reads older entries (standard UX)?" — Answer: **Not asked; assumed yes.** The existing `logAutoScroll` mechanism and `handleLogWheel` already implement this; the fix merely restores its initial state. Source: code inspection of `refreshLog`/`handleLogWheel`.
---
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSRGVGU40044GJ0** – Undo/redo feedback notification (completed)
- **CG-0MSAZL6O2008PTWY** – [test-failure] Replay CLI tests in tests/replay/replay.test.ts (spawnSync node --import tsx/esm scripts/replay.ts exceeds 15s) — failing test (completed)
- **CG-0MSLXJCHH001DLIO** – Remove time-limited play mechanics (maxTurns) (completed)

# Problem Statement

When a business card is upgraded (e.g., Bakery → Patisserie), the card's displayed name overlay always shows the original business name ("Bakery") instead of the upgraded name ("Patisserie"). This is a visual bug that misrepresents the current state of the business on the street grid.

# Users & User Stories

- **As a player**, I want the upgraded business name to be displayed on the card so I can clearly see which version of the business I have.
- **As a player**, I expect the card to show "Patisserie" after applying the "Upgrade to Patisserie" card to my Bakery, not "Bakery" as it did before.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. When an upgrade is applied to a business card, the name overlay on the card reflects the upgraded name (e.g., "Patisserie" instead of "Bakery").
2. The upgraded name is computed dynamically from the applied upgrade cards — no hard-coded name values on BusinessCard instances.
3. Multi-level upgrades display the name from the **most recently applied** upgrade (set in `displayName` each time `purchaseUpgrade()` runs).
4. Base (un-upgraded) cards display their original `name` as before — no overlay shown.
5. The fix works for all business upgrade paths in the game (Bakery→Patisserie, Diner→Bistro, etc.)
6. `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec` unit tests cover both base cards (no name overlay) and upgraded cards (correct upgraded name displayed).
7. All existing tests pass after the change.

# Constraints

- The `BusinessCard.name` field is `readonly` in the TypeScript interface — the fix must not make it mutable. A separate display-name mechanism is required.
- `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec()` only receives a `BusinessCard`, not the upgrade templates — the display name must be pre-computed and stored on the BusinessCard during `purchaseUpgrade()`.
- The fix should be minimal: touch only the BusinessCard interface, `purchaseUpgrade()`, and `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec()`.
- The solution must be data-driven where possible (driven by CSV card data), not hard-coded logic.

# Existing State

- `BusinessCard` has a `readonly name: string` (original business name) and `level: number` (upgrade level), plus `appliedUpgrades: string[]` (IDs of applied upgrades).
- `UpgradeCard` has a `name: string` (e.g., "Upgrade to Patisserie") and `targetBusiness: string` (e.g., "Bakery").
- `purchaseUpgrade()` in `MainStreetMarket.ts` updates `business.level`, `incomeBonus`, `synergyRangeBonus`, `reputationBonus`, and `appliedUpgrades` — but **never updates any display name**.
- `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec()` in `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` computes the name overlay text as `biz.name` (the original, un-upgraded name).
- Card data CSV column `name` on upgrade cards uses format "Upgrade to <new name>" (e.g., "Upgrade to Patisserie").

# Desired Change

Add a `displayName` field to `BusinessCard` and populate it when upgrades are applied:

1. Add `displayName?: string` (optional) to the `BusinessCard` interface.
2. Add a `newDisplayName` field to the `UpgradeCard` interface and CSV column, storing the business's new name directly (e.g., "Patisserie").
3. In `purchaseUpgrade()`, after applying the upgrade, set `business.displayName = card.newDisplayName`.
4. In `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec()`, use `biz.displayName ?? biz.name` for the name overlay text.

This is a single-source-of-truth approach: each upgrade card declares the new business name, and the BusinessCard tracks its current display name.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — `UpgradeCard` interface (add field)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec()` (compute name from applied upgrades)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `applyUpgradeOverlays()` (uses spec from above; likely no change needed)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — `purchaseUpgrade()` (may need to store new name on BusinessCard, depending on approach)
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — upgrade card definitions (add `newDisplayName` column if Option A)
- `example-games/main-street/tests/UpgradeOverlaySpec.test.ts` — unit tests for overlay spec

# Related Work

- **CG-0MSKSJ9SS0069ZWT**: Main Street tutorial: full text review and step restructure (references patisserie upgrade in tutorial context).

---

# Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should the BusinessCard.name field be updated, or should a separate display name mechanism be used?"
  - A: A separate display name mechanism is needed since `BusinessCard.name` is `readonly` and used for identification/logic elsewhere. The overlay should derive the display name from applied upgrades.
  - Evidence: TypeScript interface definition in `MainStreetCards.ts` line 234 (`readonly name: string`).

- Q: "Should the new name come from the upgrade card's name field, or a dedicated field?"
  - A: A dedicated field (`newDisplayName` on UpgradeCard) is preferred for clarity and to avoid fragile string parsing of "Upgrade to X" patterns.
  - Evidence: CSV data shows upgrade names as "Upgrade to Patisserie" — the new name is embedded but not cleanly extractable without parsing.

# Tooltips for Business Cards Do Not Work Reliably

## Problem Statement

Business card tooltips in Main Street are unreliable in two scenarios: (1) tooltips are suppressed when there are no actions remaining and the player hovers over a market business card, and (2) tooltips do not appear at all for business cards in the hand.

## Users

- **Main Street player (desktop):** Hovering over business cards in the market or hand should display a tooltip with card details (name, cost, income, synergy, description) so the player can make informed decisions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Business cards in the market:** Hovering over a business card in the market row displays the card tooltip with full details (name, cost, income, synergy, description) — regardless of whether actions remain. When no actions remain, the card is dimmed (alpha 0.45) but still shows its full tooltip.
2. **Business cards in the hand:** Hovering over a business card in the player's hand displays the card tooltip with full details, consistent with event card tooltips in the hand.
3. **Event card tooltips unchanged:** Existing event card tooltip behavior (market and hand) is not affected by the fix.
4. **Replay mode:** Tooltips are suppressed in replay mode, as before.
5. **All project tests pass** after the fix.

## Constraints

- Fix must be surgical — only touch tooltip event handlers, not click/drag behavior.
- Must respect `s.replayMode` flag (suppress tooltips during replay).
- Must respect the settings store tooltip toggle.
- No new dependencies or architectural changes.

## Existing State

### Market business cards (`MainStreetRenderer.ts`)

Normal business card path (no actions): `pointerover`/`pointerout` attached to `selection` or `hitArea` — tooltip works.

When `noActions` is true (line ~1268-1280):
- `container.setAlpha(0.45)` and `container.setInteractive({ useHandCursor: false })`
- `pointerover`/`pointerout` re-attached with a different message ("No actions remaining...")
- **Problem:** `setInteractive({ useHandCursor: false })` may prevent pointer events from firing. Additionally, the `pointerover`/`pointerout` handlers are re-attached, overwriting the earlier tooltip handlers.

### Hand business cards (`MainStreetRenderer.ts` line ~171-205)

Event cards in the hand get a `hover` rectangle with `pointerover`/`pointerout` → tooltip.

Business cards in the hand (`else` branch): only a `hitArea` with `pointerdown` for selection. **No `pointerover`/`pointerout` handlers → tooltips never fire.**

## Desired Change

1. **Market (no actions):** Replace the separate `noActions` tooltip override with a conditional in the existing tooltip logic — show the full card tooltip, but display a secondary note below it when actions are exhausted (or show the card tooltip + dimmed visual without replacing it).
2. **Hand business cards:** Add `pointerover`/`pointerout` handlers (a small invisible `hover` rectangle, like the event card path) that call `buildCardTooltipInfo()` and show the tooltip via `s.tooltipManager`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Market and hand business card tooltip event handlers
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — `buildCardTooltipInfo()` (already supports business cards)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** `setInteractive({ useHandCursor: false })` may or may not suppress pointer events depending on Phaser version — developer should verify this behavior in their environment before deciding on the fix approach.
- **Risk:** The hand `renderCard` function returns a container; adding hover rectangles may need careful depth management to avoid blocking upgrade overlays.
- **Assumption:** `buildCardTooltipInfo()` already returns correct content for business cards (verified: it does).
- **Assumption:** The `noActions` tooltip path was introduced to communicate the constraint (no actions left) but inadvertently broke the tooltip. Fix should preserve this communication while restoring the full card tooltip.
- **Scope creep risk:** Community-space and upgrade cards in the hand may also lack tooltips — file as a separate follow-up work item, not within this scope.
- **Scope creep risk:** Tooltips on the street (placed business cards) are handled separately and are outside this scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: What tooltip content should display for business cards with no actions remaining? — Answer: The full card tooltip (same as when actions remain), not just "No actions remaining". The dimmed visual already communicates the constraint. Source: code review of MainStreetRenderer.ts.
- Q: Should hand business card tooltips include synergy detail lines like market tooltips? — Answer: No — market tooltips use `includeEventDetail: true`, but hand tooltips (per event card precedent) use the default `includeEventDetail: false`. Source: MainStreetRenderer.ts line 1232 vs 1252.

# Intake Brief: Main Street — Action Banking

## Problem statement

Main Street's action economy (CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R) gives players `actionsRemaining` actions each day, but every unused action is lost at day end. Players have no incentive to conserve actions for a later, bigger decision. Action banking lets unused actions accumulate across days (capped at 2 banked), enabling multi-day planning.

## Users

- **Players** of Main Street — they can now save actions across days to set up a bigger play (e.g., bank two actions then execute a move-to-hand + buy-and-place combo, or afford a premium play), turning "waste or use" into a strategic reserve.
- **TCE developers / producers** — need the banking mechanic enforced consistently in state, engine, commands, save/load, and UI so it is testable and does not regress the existing action economy.

Example user stories:
- "As a player, I want to end a quiet day without acting and start the next day with my saved action so I can plan a two-action combo."
- "As a player, I want a simple counter telling me how many actions I have banked so I know my reserve at a glance."
- "As a player with a General Manager employed, I want my extra GM action spent first so I can still bank my base action when I don't use it all."

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. **Banking on end-of-turn:** When the player ends a day (End Turn), every unspent action in the day's budget banks into a `bankedActions` counter (bounded by the cap). Actions bank whether zero, some, or nearly-all actions were taken (e.g., 3 available, 1 taken → 2 banked).
- 2. **Cap enforced:** `bankedActions` never exceeds 2 — further accumulation is discarded; the bank cannot grow past the cap.
- 3. **Day-start composition:** At DayStart, the day's budget is `1 base + staff actionsPerTurn bonus + bankedActions (capped 2)`. Banked reserves are consumed as the player spends actions during the day (spending draws down the combined budget).
- 4. **Staff actions used first:** Staff-derived actions (e.g., General Manager's +1 `actionsPerTurn`) are consumed before the base/banked pool; staff bonuses themselves never bank.
- 5. **UI indicator + tooltip:** HUD shows a simple banked-action count; the action tooltip explains "1 action per turn, with up to two turns' unused actions banked", including the General Manager +1 note when a GM is employed.
- 6. **State + persistence:** `bankedActions` round-trips through save/load (legacy saves default to 0), and is included in undo/redo command snapshot/restore (pattern mirroring `actionsRemaining`).
- 7. **Quality gates:** Unit tests cover banking accumulation, cap enforcement, staff-first ordering, day-start composition, save/load round-trip, and undo/redo; `npm test` passes and `npm run build` succeeds; related docs updated.

## Constraints

- **Main Street only** — no core-engine changes.
- **Bank cap fixed at 2** per operator decision (the initial seed context said 4; superseded). Max budget on any day = 1 base + staff bonus + 2 banked.
- Bank resets to 0 at new game; banked actions never expire except through spending.
- Tutorial coverage is a **separate follow-up item** (CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P) — out of scope here.
- Banking-aware AI strategy (deliberate hoarding) is a **separate follow-up item** (CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W) — out of scope here. In-scope AI behavior is passive: the AI consumes whatever budget it is given; banking accrues only when the AI happens to end a day with leftovers.
- Scope-creep guard: rebalancing the action economy, changing the cap, or redesigning the HUD layout are out of scope; record as discussion, not implementation.

## Existing state

- `state.actionsRemaining` is reset to `1 + gmBonus` at every DayStart in `executeDayStart` (MainStreetEngine.ts:851); every action-type command decrements it and throws when it is ≤ 0 (MainStreetEngine.ts:257-274, MainStreetCommands.ts:35-38).
- `actionsRemaining` is serialized/deserialized in MainStreetState.ts (line ~827) with a legacy backfill default of 1 (line ~981-983) and is part of the undo/redo command snapshot in MainStreetCommands.ts (line ~52/84/103).
- General Manager (`staff-general-manager`) grants `actionsPerTurn: 1` via the `actionsPerTurn` staff ability (shipped with CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R).
- The HUD action counter and tooltips live in `MainStreetRenderer.ts` / `MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`; tutorial copy in `TutorialFlow.ts` / `TutorialScenario.ts`.

## Desired change

Add a `bankedActions` field to Main Street state, computed at day end from unspent budget (capped at 2, staff-first consumption), composed into the day-start budget, surfaced in the HUD counter and tooltip, and persisted through save/load and undo/redo. Tutorial and banking-aware AI behavior are tracked as separate follow-up items.

## Key Files
